doc.title: Janis Siegel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 22, 2015

title: Producer Joel Dorn and her first Atlantic solo record
summary: She sought out Joel Dorn for her 1981 Atlantic record with an eclectic cassette; they became friends, and he gave her Joe Williams' shirt.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I wanted to throw out a name that you know, Joel Dorn?

Yeah, he is one of the great ones. I sought him out. When I was about to do my first solo record for Atlantic in 1981 I gave some thought to it and I thought I’m just going to go through my collection and see who I like. And I picked out like Roberta Flack’s record and Bette Midler’s first record and there were some other things, and the Neville Brothers and then Freddie Hubbard and then this and that and this from Atlantic and I went I think Joel Dorn might be a good guy to talk to. So I made a cassette — that’s how long ago it was — of tunes that I wanted to do, and he was very intrigued by it because it was very
eclectic and that’s what he liked. And I had things by the Dixie Hummingbirds on there and I had vocalese and I had some pop things, and he liked that a lot.
Was he affiliated with any record labels at the time?
Yes. And that was a relationship that I treasured. And I think we were just becoming really good friends when he passed, I mean just gone. One day here, next day gone.
Yeah, I learned of him sort of after the fact of records that I liked and then I started to see his name on this one and then Hubert Laws.
Yes. Well Rahsaan Roland Kirk. He was the man.
And he loved Joe Williams. When Joe passed, he was friends with Joe’s widow I believe and Joel gave me one of Joe’s shirts, I think I told you that, which I still have at home.
